newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to give Magic Johnson guarded welcome.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to give Magic Johnson guarded welcome.

text.p: Indonesian Health Minister Suyudi said on Monday HIV-positive U.S. basketball star Earvin "Magic" Johnson, who arrives in Jakarta this week, should be "guarded" so that he does not spread his disease.

"The department of health supports the arrival of Magic Johnson in order to lift the ability of basketball in Indonesia," Suyudi told the official Antara news agency at parliament after the annual budget speech.
"But the community needs to be given information about the spread of HIV/AIDS so that this athlete who is HIV positive can be guarded in order that he does not spread his disease," he said.

HIV, the virus that causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), is transferred through sexual contact, blood transfusion, through the re-use of medical instruments such as needles or through pregnant mothers to their unborn children.
Suyudi said Indonesian's were being educated through brochures, books, a telephone hotline and training of health personnel.
Johnson, who was due to arrive in Jakarta on Tuesday, was denied a visa to enter Indonesia in 1994 because of his illness.
He was last month issued with a visa in Los Angeles to visit Indonesia to hold an exhibition match in Jakarta this week.

The news agency quoted the director-general of infectious diseases, Hadi Abednego, as saying the department had no concerns with Johnson's visit as long as he was accompanied by a medical team from the local department of health while he played.
The World Health Organisation has said as many as 500,000 Indonesians might be infected with the virus.
Indonesia has put the number of HIV or AIDS-related deaths at 465, but health workers said that figure represented only reported cases and the real number could be up to a hundred times greater.
Indonesia has a population of nearly 200 million people, making it the world's fourth most populous nation.
